θρίδαξ.definition: Ion. and Dor. for lettuce, Epich.158, Hdt.3.32, Hp.Mul.1.78, Thphr.HP7.2.4, BGU 1118.13 , IG4.955.8 , etc.:—also POxy.1212 ; Hsch. s.v. Epich. l.c., AP9.412 , 11.295 , 413 , cf. the accentuation lacks authority.]

Θρινακίη.definition: a legendary island, Od.11.107, etc.: afterwards identified with Sicily and written ; cf. Str.6.2.1:—Adj. Sicilian, Nic.Th.529

θρῖναξ.definition: trident, three-pronged fork, used to stir grain, etc., Ar.Pax567, Nic.Th.114, PFay.120.3 ; as a signet, Tab.Heracl.1.5. later AP6.95 codd. .]

θρίξ.definition: gen. dat. pl. : - hair, Hom. only in pl., . . Il.24.359; mostly, hair of the head, 22.77, Od.13.431; Th.1.6; sheep’s wool, Il.3.273, Hes.Op.517; pig’s bristles, Il.19.254, Od.10.239; of a horse’s tail, Il.23.519; of a…

θριοβόλος.definition: one who throws pebbles into the divining-urn, soothsayer, Epic. ap. St.Byz. s.v. Suid

θρῖον.definition: fig-leaf, Ar.Ec.707, Sotad.Com.1.27; prov., of empty threats, Ar.V.436

θριπήδεστος.definition: seals made of worm-eaten wood, Ar.Th.427, cf. Sch; metaph., = Hyp.Fr.82. , Hyp. l.c. , Luc.Lex.13 , cf. Paus.Gr.Fr.205, but a Sup. is never necessary exc. in Thphr.HP3.8.5 .)

θρίσσα.definition: Att. a fish, = Anaxandr.41.52, Ephipp.12.5, Arist.HA621b16, PCair.Zen.40 , al., Gp.20.7.1: BGU816.20 : is v.l. in AP6.304

θρόδαξ.definition: Cypr. for Id.:—Dim. Choerob. in An.Ox. 2.218

θρόνον.definition: only in pl. flowers embroidered on; herbs used as drugs and charms, Theoc.2.59, Nic.Th.493,936, Lyc.674, Aglaïas7; used in sacrificial offering, UPZ96.4

θρόνος.definition: seat, chair, Od.1.145, Ath.5.192e, PMasp.6; throne, chair of state, Hdt.1.14, cf. X.HG1.5.3, etc.; Theoc.7.93: metaph., Pl.R.553c: pl., A.Ch.975; Id.Pr.910; S.Ant.1041, cf. Ar.Av.1732; king's estate or dignity, S.OC42…

θρόνωσις.definition: = enthronement of the newly initiated, at the mysteries of the Corybantes, Pl.Euthd.277d

θρόος.definition: Att. noise as of many; murmur of a crowd or assembly, Th.4.66, 8.79, D.H.6.57, etc

θρύαλλον.definition: shower of smuts from a distant bonfire, Vett.Val.345.22

θρῦλος.definition: noise as of many voices, murmur, Batr.135, Orph.Fr.286 , Demetr.Lac.Herc.1786.1 F., Anon. ap.Suid.—This word and its cognates are written with one in Papyri and best codd. , with in inferior codd., also in PLips.40 ii 10

θρύμμα.definition: that which is broken off, bit, Hp.Mul.1.75, Ar.Fr.160, Aglaïas20, Gal.6.343; AP6.232

θρυμματίς.definition: a sort of cake, Antiph.183.4, Philox.2.18, Luc.Lex.6

θρύον.definition: reed, rush, Il.21.351, Hp.Steril.246; = thornapple, Datura Stramonium, Orph.A.916, Thphr.HP9.11.6 , Dsc.4.73

θρύψις.definition: breaking in small pieces; softness, weakness, Plu.Dem.4: esp. metaph., debauchery, X.Cyr.8.8.16, Plu.Lyc.14: pl., Id.2.732e

θρωσμός.definition: springing; of ground rising from the plain, Il.10.160, 11.56; A.R.2.823

θυανία.definition: prob. f.l. for Dor. for Epich.148

θυγάτηρ.definition: gen. contr. dat; later, maidservant, slave, Phalar.Ep.142.3. in Ep. in the longer forms, metri gr.]

θυείδιον.definition: Dim. of Ar.Pl.710; wrongly written in cod. Rav., as in Damocr. ap. Gal.14.118

θυηπόλος.definition: also Suid., performing sacrifices, sacrificial, A.Pers.202: Subst., diviner, soothsayer, E.IA746, Ar.Pax1124; priest, IG3.1337.9, cf. Phld.D.1.4; of the Vestal Virgins, D.H.2.64, al

θύϊνος.definition: of the tree , Str.4.6.2, v.l. in Dsc.1.22; made of this wood, Callix.1, Apoc.18.12

θυΐσκη.definition: censer, LXX1 Ma.1.22, al., J.AJ3.6.8, v.l., ib.3.6.8:—also POxy.1657.13 , Suid., EM458.53: ib.52

θύλακος.definition: sack, esp. to carry meal in; sack in which the eggs of the tunny are enveloped, Arist.HA571a14, cf. 552b19

θῦλαξ.definition: = Arcesil.Com.1 D., Aesop.15;= Hsch.; cited fr. Hom. by Poll.10.172; cj. in Sor.1.57

θῦμα.definition: victim, sacrifice, SIG56.31; metaph., of persons, prob. of Clytemnestra, A.Ag.1118 ; Hdn.2.13.5

θυμάλωψ.definition: piece of burning wood or charcoal, Ar.Ach.321, Th.729, Stratt.55, Luc.Lex.24

θύμβρα.definition: savory, Satureia Thymbra, Eup.14.5, Thphr.CP3.1.4, Dsc.3.37, Plin.HN19.165:—also Hp. ap.Gal.19.104

θυμβρεπίδειπνος.definition: supping on bitter herbs, i.e. living poorly, Ar.Nu.421

Θύμβρις.definition: name of several rivers, esp. the Tiber, AP9.352 , D.P.352 sq.; cf

θυμβροφάγος.definition: eating savory, to look as if one had eaten savory, 'make a verjuice face', Ar.Ach.254

θυμελαία.definition: prob. spurge-flax, Daphne Cnidium, Dsc.4.172, Plin. HN13.114:—hence wine flavoured with Dsc.5.68

θύμον.definition: a marine plant, Id.HP4.7.2; mixture of thyme with honey and vinegar, eaten by the poor of Attica, Ar.Pl.253, cf. 283, Antiph.226.7, Luc.Fug.14, Hsch

θύμος.definition: [perh. , warty excrescence, Hp.Alim.17; the thymus gland in the neck or breast of young animals, Ruf.Onom.168, Gal.UP6.4

θυμός.definition: soul, spirit, as the principle of life, feeling and thought, esp. of strong feeling and passion by Pl.Cra.419e I. in physical sense, breath, life, freq. in Hom., Il.6.17, 5.852, 155, 1.205: c. dupl. acc., 6.17; . . 22…

θυμοφόρος.definition: bearing thyme, Eust.ad D.P.791; Sch. Ar.Pl.283

θύννος.definition: tunny-fish, Orac. ap. Hdt.1.62, A.Pers.424, Arist.HA571a12, al., Ath.7.301e sqq.; Phld.Rh.1.251S

θύον.definition: thyine-wood, citron-wood; = in pl. burnt-offerings or incense, Sapph.Supp.8.2, prob. in IG5.p.vii , Pi.Fr.129.7 , BCH37.195 , SIG1003.10 , D.P.936, EM457.6

θύος.definition: burnt sacrifice, A.Ag.1409; later in pl., = Hp. ap. Gal.19.104

θύρα.definition: Ion. Ion. gen. pl; esp. of kings and potentates, are educated at court, X.An.1.9.3; of a petitioner, Hdt.3.119, cf. X.An.2.1.8; dangling after the court, Id.HG1.6.7; Arist.Rh.1391a12; Id.Pol.1313b7, Theopomp.Hist.121;…

θυραμάχος.definition: assaulting doors, prob. l. in Pratin.Lyr.1.8

θυρεαμαχία.definition: contest in which shields were borne, SIG1061.12

θυρεός.definition: stone put against a door to keep it; oblong shield , PSI4.428.36 , Inscr. ap. Plu.Pyrrh.26, Callix.2; hence, of the Roman scutum , Plb.2.30.3, 6.23.2, D.H.4.16, cf.Ep.Eph.6.16, Apollod.Poliorc.163.2, Arr.Tact.3.2, etc

θυρεπανοίκτης.definition: door-opener, of the philosopher Crates, for whom all doors were open, Plu.2.632e; or, who forced all doors, D.L.6.86: pl., burglars, Vett.Val.202.6; cf

θυρίς.definition: Dim. of window, Praxill.5; audience-window of the king or high officials in Egypt, UPZ15.7, 16.20, 53.5 , Heraclid.Cum.4

θυριώτης.definition: one found at the door, Suid

Θυρξεύς.definition: title of Apollo in Achaea, Paus.7.21.13

θυροειδής.definition: like a door, dub. in Hippiatr.40 ; the opening in the os pubis, Gal.2.414

θυροκρουστία.definition: knocking at a door, dub. in Sammelb.4425 ii 24

θυροφύλαξ.definition: door-keeper, Sch.Il.22.69, prob. in Fronto Epig.Gr.5.1

θυρσίων.definition: part of a fish, Ath.7.310e; Lat. tursio , = a dolphin-like fish, Plin.HN9.34

θύρσος.definition: in late Poets with heterocl. pl

θύσανος.definition: tassel: mostly in pl., tassels, fringe, Hom. , of the tassels of the 2.448; 14.181, cf. Hes.Sc.225, Hdt.4.189; Ach.Tat.5.24; Them.Or.18.222c; of the tufts of the golden fleece, Pi.P.4.231; of the long arms of the cutt…

θύσιμος.definition: fit for sacrifice, Hdt.1.50, cf. Ar.Ach.784; Plu.2.437a, cf. Porph.Abst.2.14

θυστάς.definition: sacrificial, the cry; as Subst., = Sch.Opp.H.5.417;= Hsch

Θυώνη.definition: epith. of Semele, h.Hom.1.21; Dor. portion of sacrifice, acc. pl. Abh. Berl.Akad. 1928.12 ; cf. Hsch. s.v

θωή.definition: penalty, Od.2.192; a penalty imposed by them, Il.13.669:—Att. IG12.114.42:— Ion. also Archil.109, BCH50.214 , prob. l. in Democr.262: SIG58.12 : Att. gen. pl. with acc. to Choerob.in Theod.1.405, but v. supr. and cf

θῶμιγξ.definition: cord, string, Hdt.1.199, AP9.343 , Polyaen.6.50, Ael.VH3.26; bow-string, A.Pers.461, Eu.182, Trag.Adesp.215; a fishing-line, Opp.H.3.76, etc

θωμός.definition: heap, A.Ag.295, Ar.Lys.973, Thphr.HP8.11.4, AP6.299 : metaph., Ar.Fr.217

θωρηκτής.definition: armed with Il.21.429; armed with stout cuirass, 12.317,15.689

θώρηξις.definition: drinking to intoxication, Hp.Aph.2.21, 7.48, Gal.17.498, 18.154, Aret.SD2.6: pl., Hp.Morb.2.66

θώς.definition: also prob. jackal, Canis aureus; hunting dog, Lycaon pictus, Opp.C.3.338, al

θώψ.definition: gen. flatterer, false friend, Hdt.3.80; as Adj., fawning speeches, Trag.Adesp.24, Pl.Tht.175e, Ph.2.52

θαάσσω.definition: Ep. form of used only in pres. and impf., sit, Il.9.194, cf. 15.124; . . Od.3.336, cf. h.Merc.172; ib.468

θαέομαι.definition: Dor. for , Pi.P.8.45: aor. 1 Lyr.Adesp.40; imper. Epigr. ap. Phan.Hist.12; cf

θακέω.definition: Ion. and Dor. impf. Cratin.239: Dor. fut. Epich.99.1:—sit, Hdt.2.173; Sophr.60; . . A.Pr.315; S.Aj.325· . . E.Hec.1153: c. acc. cogn., sitting on imperial throne, A.Pr.391; of suppliants, S.OT20, Aj.1173; E.Heracl.239

θάκησις.definition: means of sitting, seat, prob. in S.OC9

θαλαμαῖος.definition: shut up, kept at home, Ph.2.297

θαλαμεύω.definition: lead into the i.e. take to wife, Hld.4.6:—Pass., of women, to be shut up, kept at home, Aristaenet.2.5; to be taken to wife, Ph.1.323

θαλάμη.definition: lurking-place, den, lair; of cavities in the body, Hp.de Arte10 ; ventricle of the heart, Arist.Somn.Vig.458a17; of the pores of sponges, Id.HA548a28; the nostrils, Poll.2.79; of the optic thalamus, Gal.UP16.3; of rec…

θαλαμηϊάδης.definition: son of the or hole, comic patron. of the tunny, MatroConv.53

θαλαμηπολέω.definition: to be a Sch.Lyc.132; put to the stud, of animals, Opp.C.1.393

θαλαμηπόλος.definition: attendant in a lady's; in later Gr., eunuch of the bedchamber, Plu.Alex.30, Agath.1.7; of the Galli or eunuch-priests of Cybele, AP6.220 ; but also a priestess of Cybele, Rhian.67.1

θαλαμίτης.definition: one of the rowers on the lowest bench of a trireme, who had the shortest oars and the least pay, Sch.Ar.Ra.1106

θαλασσερός.definition: a kind of eyesalve, Gal.12.781, etc

θαλασσίζω.definition: resemble sea-water, Diph.Siph. ap; wash in sea-water, PHolm.17.2

θαλάσσιος.definition: later Att. also; skilled in the sea, nautical, Hdt.7.144; Th.1.142

θαλασσίτης.definition: wine sunk in the sea, to ripen it, Plin.HN14.78

θαλασσοβίωτος.definition: living on or by the sea, App.Pun.89:—also Sch.Opp.H.2.1

θαλασσοβραχής.definition: soaked in brine, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.12.3

θαλασσοειδής.definition: like the sea, sea-green, Hp.Vid.Ac.1, Democr. Eph.1, Str.17.1.35; HeroAut.30.6

θαλασσόκλυστος.definition: dashed by the sea, Sch.Barocc. S.Aj.696

θαλασσοκοπέω.definition: strike the sea with the oar, make a splash, metaph.in Ar.Eq.830, Lib.Decl.26.18

θαλασσοκρατέω.definition: to be master of the sea, Hdt.3.122, Th.7.48, Plb.1.7.6, Phylarch.1 J.:—Pass., to be beaten at sea, Demetr.Com. Vet.2

θαλασσοκράτωρ.definition: master of the sea, Hdt.5.83, Th.8.63, X.HG1.6.2

θαλασσομέδων.definition: lord of the sea, Nonn.D.21.95: Lacon. fem. Alcm.84

θαλασσόμελι.definition: drink of brine and honey, Dsc.5.12

θαλασσονόμος.definition: dwelling in the sea, Emp.76.1, Nonn.D.37.265

θαλασσόπλαγκτος.definition: made to wander o'er the sea, seatost, of ships, A.Pr.467; of a corpse, E.Hec.782:—also Sch.Opp.H.4.582

θαλασσουργέω.definition: to be busy with the sea, Plb.6.52.1, Str.6.1.1, Max. Tyr.22.3, etc

θαλασσουργία.definition: business on the sea, fishing, etc., Hp.Vict.3.68 , Them.Or.24.305d

θαλασσουργός.definition: one who works on the sea, a fisherman or sailor, Charon10, X.Oec.16.7, Plb.10.8.5: as Adj., Philostr.VA4.32

θαλασσόω.definition: Att. make or change into sea; purify with sea-water, Hsch

θαλέθω.definition: poet. for , bloom, thrive, used by Hom. only in part., . . Od.23.191, cf. Ibyc.1.6, A.R.2.843; Emp.20.3; of men, Od.6.63; IG14.1363; AP11.374 ; Lyr.Adesp.98 ; swelling, wantoning in fat, Il.9.467, cf. 23.32: c. acc., …

θαλέω.definition: = Q.S.11.96 codd., Nonn.D.16.78; Hp.Insomn.90; v.l. for in Mosch.2.67

θαλιάζω.definition: enjoy oneself, make merry, Plu.2.746f, al. ; Polyaen.4.15

θαλλοφόρος.definition: carrying young olive-shoots, as the old men did at the Panathenaea, Ar.V.544 , X.Smp.4.17; as a name of Heracles, IG 14.904

θάλλω.definition: Hes.Op.173, h.Cer.402, etc.: aor.1; of other natural objects, copious dew, Od.13.245; rich with fat, Il.9.208, cf. Od.13.410; at a sumptuous feast, 11.415

θαλπιάω.definition: to be or become warm, right warm and comfortable, Od.19.319, cf. Arat.1073

θάλπος.definition: warmth, heat, esp. summer-heat, opp; metaph., sting, smart, S.Ant.1086; of love, AP6.207

θάλπω.definition: fut. Orph.Fr.258, Alciphr.2.4: fut. Med. in; heat, warm, without any notion of softening, S.Ant.417; Ar.Av.1092; keep warm, Trag.Adesp.7: prov., of an idle life, Herod.1.37; Id.7.48; ib.129:—Pass., Hp.Aff.4; to be war…

θαλπωρή.definition: warming: metaph., comfort, consolation, Il.6.412, cf. Od.1.167; IG4.623 : pl., Tryph.128.—In late Prose, Jul.Or.8.243c

θαμβαίνω.definition: = to be astonished at, Pi.O.3.32, v.l. for in h.Ven.84

θαμβέω.definition: to be astounded; c. acc., to be astonished at, Od.2.155, cf. 16.178; Pi.N.3.50; A.Supp.570 : in late Prose, Plu.Aem.34

θαμβήτειρα.definition: the fearful one, of the Furies, Orph.A.973

θαμβόομαι.definition: to be terrified, pf. part. Aët.16.66

θάμβος.definition: also Simon.237, LXXEc.12.5; in objective sense, terrors in the way, LXX l.c.; object of wonder, Epigr.Gr.1068

θαμίζω.definition: to be accustomed: c.part., he was not wont to be so cared for, Od.8.451; we do not often see you coming down, Pl.R.328c; mourns constantly, S.OC672 : abs., by dint of repetition, Pl.Lg.843b

θαμνίσκος.definition: Dim. of Dsc.4.108, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.8.4.6, Gal.2.355

θαμυρίζω.definition: assemble, Hsch.; take part in a meeting, BCH50.401 ; assembly, Hsch

θανατάω.definition: Desiderat. of desire to die; to be moribund, Ph.2.505, Lyd.Mag.3.40, v.l. in 45

θανατήσιος.definition: = rejected by Poll.5.132 , but found in Afric.Cest.14, 16, 17 ; cf. Phot.; AB99

θανατηφόρος.definition: death-bringing, A.Ch.369 ; cycle of mortality, Pl.R.617d; of hurts or accidents, Hp.Art.48; of a surgical operation, Antyll. ap. Orib.45.17.6; of arrow-poison, Acokanthera Schimperi, Thphr.HP9.15.2; Arist.PA672a36; . …

θανατόω.definition: fut. A.Pr.1053 , etc.: pf; Pass., of flesh, to be mortified, Hp.Fract.26:—metaph. in Act., mortify, Ep.Rom.8.13

θάπτω.definition: fut. Is.8.21:—Pass., fut. E.Alc.632, Lys.13.45, also S.Aj.577, 1141, E.IT1464: aor. 1 Simon.167 , Hdt.2.81,7.228; more freq.aor. 2 Id.3.10, 55, and always in Att., as Ar.Pl.556; part. CIG2839 : pf. Ion.3pl. v.l. Hdt.6…

θαρσαλέος.definition: in bad sense, overbold, audacious, Od.17.449; 19.91; Pl.Lg.649c. Adv., Is.10.1

θαρσαλεότης.definition: Att. boldness, confidence, Andronic.Rhod.p.578M., Plu.Aem.36,2.443d, Jul.Or.3.107b, Them.Or.2.30b; opp. Ph.1.476

θαρσέω.definition: abs., Il.l.c., etc.; fear not! 4.184, A.Supp.732, etc.; ib.600,910; Sopat.14; Ar.Pl.328, al.:—in Epitaphs, . . CIG5200b , etc.: part. in an adverb. sense, with good courage, Il.1.85, cf. A.Ch.666; Id.Ag.1671, cf. Pr.9…

θάρσησις.definition: confidence in a thing, f.l. in Th.7.49

θάσσω.definition: Ep. , sit, sit idle, E.Supp.391; Id.Ba.622 ; Id.Rh.509; Id.Hec.36; Id.IT1253 ; Id.HF715: c. acc. sedis, S.OT161 ; E.Ion91 ; Id.Andr.117 : c. acc. cogn., to sit in wretched posture, Id.HF1214, cf. Ar.Th.889. : v

θαυμάζω.definition: Ion. Att. fut. A.Pr.476; abs., wonder, marvel, Il.24.394, Pl.Hp.Ma.282e, etc

θαυμαίνω.definition: Ep. fut. = 2, admire; abs., wonder, , . . Archyt. ap. eund.3.1.114

θαύμακτρον.definition: money paid to see conjurers' tricks, Sophr.120

θαυμάσιος.definition: Adv. wonderfully, i.e. exceedingly, Ar.Nu.1240: freq. with marvellously wretched, Pl.Grg.471a; I should be wonderfully cautious, D.29.1

θαυμασιότης.definition: disposition to wonder; marvellous nature or quality, Clearch.69

θαυμασιουργία.definition: jugglery. Philostr.VA6.10: metaph., wizardry of language, Phld.Rh.2.94 S

θαυμασμός.definition: marvelling, Phld.Rh.2.57 S., Corn.ND2, Dius ap. Stob.4.21.16, S.E.M.9.17, Plu.Aem.39, etc

θαυμαστέος.definition: to be wondered at; neut. one must wonder, . . E.Hel.85, cf. 499, Phld.Rh.2.27 S., etc

θαυμαστής.definition: Ion. admirer, Ps.-Hdt.Vit.Hom.5 , Arist.Rh.1384b37, al., Plu.Cat.Mi.25, Ph.Byz.Mir.4.2; Phld.Vit.p.14J

θαυμαστόω.definition: magnify, LXXPs.4.4, al., EM443.37:—Pass., to be regarded as a marvel, Arist.HA633a8, cf. Plu.Per.28

θαυματοποιέω.definition: do wonders, play jugglers' tricks, Luc.Peregr.17, 21: metaph., Phld.Po.5.24, cf. Jul.Or.3.127c: c. acc., Porph.Chr.27

θαυματοποιία.definition: conjuring, juggling, Pl.R.602d; of orators, a straining after the marvellous, Isoc.10.7

θαυματουργέω.definition: = X.Smp.7.2; work wonders or miracles, Ph.2.18,185; but 'play tricks with', of Xerxes, Id.1.674; wonderful phenomena, Pl.Ti.80c

θεαγωγέω.definition: evoke gods, Iamb.Myst.3.6:—hence ib.2.10:— Adj. PMag.Par.1.975,985

θέαμα.definition: Ion. sight, spectacle, Semon.7.67, A.Pr.306, E.Supp.783, Ar.Av.1716, etc.; Pl.Com.130; opp. Th.2.39; freq. of a sight which gives pleasure, X.Smp.2.2, cf. 7.5; Phld.Mus.p.26 K.; Pl.R.440a; but also A.Pr.69, cf. S.Aj.9…

θεάομαι.definition: Ep. and Ion. , Dor; of the mind, contemplate, Pl.Phd.84b, al

θεατής.definition: Ion. one who sees or goes to see, Hdt.3.139, cf. E.Ion301; in the theatre, spectator, Ar.Nu.575, al.; Th.3.38; one who contemplates, Arist.EN1098a31

θεατρίζω.definition: to be or play on the stage, Suid; Pass., to be made a show of, held up to shame, Ep.Hebr.10.33

θεατροειδής.definition: like a theatre, Str.4.1.4, cf. D.S.19.45. Adv. Str.16.2.41; like the spectators in a theatre, Crito ap.Gal.12.458

θεατροκοπία.definition: courting of applause, in pl., Artem.2.70

θεατροκρατία.definition: rule exercised by the spectators in a theatre, Pl.Lg.701a

θεατροκυνηγέσιον.definition: in pl., beast-hunts in the amphitheatre, Ausonia6.9* , Just.Nov.105.1:—also ibid

θεατρομανέω.definition: to be mad after stage-plays, Man.4.277, Ph.2.167

θρησκεύω.definition: perform religious observances, Hdt.2.64; c. acc., worship, D.H.2.23, IG5.268.42 , Porph.Abst.4.9, Hdn.1.11.1:—Pass., Dinon17, LXXWi.14.16, Porph. ap. Eus.PE3.11: impers., D.H.1.76

θρῆσκος.definition: religious, Ep.Jac.1.26; in bad sense, superstitious, Hsch

θριάζω.definition: to be rapt, possessed, S.Fr.466, E.Fr.478; also glossed by , Hsch.,EM455.45:—also = AB265; cf. sq

θριαμβευτής.definition: one who enjoys a triumph, Suid

θριαμβεύω.definition: pf. Id.Ant.34: :-triumph, Plb.6.53.7, Posidon.1 J., Plu.Pomp.45, etc.; triumph over, Id.Rom.25, App.Gall.1; Plu.Cor.35, cf. App.BC1.80; ib.4.31; also Hdn.3.9.1; Plu.Publ.9: c. acc. cogn., Id.2.318b; Id.Fab.23. II. lea…

θριγκίον.definition: Dim. of sq., Luc.Gall.22, App.Mith.71, Just.Nov.133.1

θριγκός.definition: topmost course of stones in a wall; metaph., coping-stone, last finish, E.Tr.489; . . Pl.R.534e

θριγκόω.definition: surround with a; build even to the coping-stone: metaph., complete, make an end of, A.Ag.1283; to bring the house to the height of misery, E.HF1280; . . Arist.Ph.246a19

θρίγκωμα.definition: coping, cornice, cj. for J.AJ15.11.3: metaph., of salt, Plu.2.685b

θριδακίνη.definition: Att. form of Ion. and Dor; wild lettuce, Lactuca Scariola, Id.l.c.; ib.9.11.10; in this signf., opp. Gal.13.387, Hellad. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.532B

θριπόβρωτος.definition: = foreg., Philosteph. ap. Hsch., Lyc.508:—a form is condemned by Hsch

θρίσσω.definition: = Ar.Byz. ap.Erot.; Ion.acc. to Greg.Cor.p.571 S

θροέω.definition: aor. poet. B.3.9, S.Aj.947; c. acc., tell out, utter aloud, Id.Ag.1137 ; ib.1141 , cf. 104; S.OC597; ib.1425.—Rare. exc. in Trag.; in late Prose, J.AJ18.6.10, 19.1.16

θρομβοειδής.definition: full of clots or lumps, Hp.Mul.1.11,38

θρομβόομαι.definition: Pass., to become clotted, curdled, of; contain clots, Hp.Mul.2.165; of the breasts, Dsc.Eup.1.128:—Act., cause to coagulate, only as v.l. in Sch.Nic.Th.709

θρόμβος.definition: lump, Hdt.1.179; clot of; drop, . . Ev.Luc.22.44

θρόμβωσις.definition: becoming curdled; blocked vein, thrombosis, Cael.Aur.TP4.40

θρονίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be enthroned, LXXEs.1.2; to be initiated, consecrated, PMag.Lond.121.747

θρόνιον.definition: Dim. of EM456.28; part of the constellation Cassiopea, Ptol.Alm.8.2

θρυαλλίς.definition: plantain, Plantago crassifolia; wick, Ar.Ach.874,al., Philyll.26

θρυγονάω.definition: tap at, Ar.Ec.34 ; perh. to be read in Pherecr.10: cf. Hsch., Theognost.Can.20

θρύϊνος.definition: rushy, Anon. ap. Suid., dub. in PFlor. 383.28

θρυλέω.definition: make a confused noise, chatter; c. acc., repeat over and over, E.El.910; . . Pl.Phd.65b; . . , Isoc.12.237; . . D.1.7, cf. 19.156; will keep talking of it, Id.21.160: abs., Epicur.Nat.109 G.; Id.Fr.423: c. inf., PSI5.…

θρυλιγμός.definition: or unmusical sound, false note, D.H.Comp.11; Porph.in Harm.p.204 W

θρύπτω.definition: aor. 1 Hp.Mul.1.75:—Pass. and; metaph. in moral sense, enfeeble, esp. by debauchery and luxury, Ti.Locr.103b; corrupt, Pl.Lg.778a, Phld.Mus.p.79K.; Jul.Or.1.10c; Ph.1.453; = , Ael.Ep.9

θρῴσκω.definition: folld. by Prep., leap upon, assault, Il.8.252, cf. 15.380; A.R.1.1296; E.Or.257 ; of a recurring illness, attack, S.Tr.1028

θυγατριδῆ.definition: daughter's daughter, granddaughter, And.1.128, Lys.32.2, D.H.Lys.21: uncontr. nom. pl. Euph.94.2

θυγατριδοῦς.definition: daughter's son, grandson, Is.8.17, Arist.Fr.473, Ph.2.82, 425, OGI529.23 : acc. as though from nom. ib.377.5 :—Ion. Hdt.5.67, 69

θυγάτριον.definition: Dim. of little daughter or girl, Stratt.63, Men.428, PPetr.3p.155 , Macho ap.Ath.13.581c, Com.Adesp.14.19 D.,SIG364.55 , Plu.Ant.33, Jul.Or.7.226b

θυγατρόγαμος.definition: married to one's own daughter, Nonn.D.12.73

θυγατρογόνος.definition: begetting or bearing daughters, ib.7.212, al

θυγατρομιξία.definition: incest with a daughter, POxy.237 vii 26

θυγατροποιία.definition: adoption of a daughter, GDI3706 vi 61 :—written IG 12.818

θύελλα.definition: hurricane, squall , Il.6.346, al.; . . Od.5.317; prob.thunderstorms, 12.68; 20.66; 10.48, cf. S.El.1151; Id.OC1660; in similes, Il.13.39; Hes.Sc.345: metaph., A.Ag.819; Phld.Rh.1.184S

θυελλοφορέομαι.definition: Pass., to be carried by a storm, D.S.16.80

θύεστον.definition: drink made from bruised spices, Hsch

θυηλή.definition: part of a victim offered in burnt- sacrifice, usu. in pl., Il.9.220, cf. Philoch.172, Nic.Fr.62, Ath.13.566a: generally, sacrifice, Ar.Av.1520; AP6.324.3 ; D.S.3.62, Porph.Abst.2.59: metaph., an offering to Ares, i.e.…

θύημα.definition: = foreg., in pl., Tim.Lex.:= Hp. ap. Erot

θυηπολέω.definition: trans., sacrifice, S.Fr.126, cf. 522, Maiist.13:—Pass., is filled with sacrifices by them, E.Heracl.401

θυηπολία.definition: Ion. sacrificing, A.R.1.1124, AP5.16 , D.H.1.21, Hld.3.2, prob. in Puchstein Epigr.Gr.36 : generally, mystic rites, Orph.A.470

θυλακίζω.definition: collect scraps in a wallet: hence, at Tarentum, beg, Hsch

θυλακίτης.definition: = sq., only fem. the common poppy , Dsc.4.64; = Id.1.9

θυλακοφορέω.definition: carry a sack or pouch, Ar.Fr.789

θυλακοφόρος.definition: carrying a bag, name for prospectors, Hsch., Phot

θυλέομαι.definition: offer in sacrifice, Porph.Abst.2.17; shd. be read in Poll.1.27

θύλημα.definition: that which is offered: mostly in pl., cakes, incense, etc., Ar.Pax1040, Thphr.Fr.97.3, Pherecr.23.6, Telecl.33, Porph.Abst.2.6, 29; cf. , Lett. dūlēt 'smoke ', Lat.fuligo.) Pherecr. l.c.]

θυμαίνω.definition: Ep.impf. A.R.3.1326: :—to be wroth, angry, Hes.Sc.262, Ar.Nu.610; at one, ib.1478, Eup.191

θυμαλγής.definition: heart-grieving, Il.4.513; Pass., inly grieving, A.Ag.1031

θυμαρής.definition: suiting the heart, i.e. well-pleasing, delightful, Il.9.336, Od.23.232; 17.199: irreg. acc. IG14.433 :—also , Hom. only in neut. as Adv., Od.10.362: as Adj., A.R.1.705; Mosch.2.29: also in later Prose, Luc.Am.43, Hdn.…

θυμέλη.definition: prop.place of burning, hearth; esp. of the altar of Dionysus which stood in the orchestra of the theatre, Pratin.Lyr.1.2, cf.EM743.37, etc.: hence in later writers

θυμηδέω.definition: Dor. , to be glad-hearted, Semon.7.103; Hld.10.3

θυμηδής.definition: well-pleasing, dear, Od.16.389; A.R.1.249; A.Supp.962; Epigr.Gr.403.7 ; cj. for in Herod.Med. ap. Orib.10.40.1

θυμηδία.definition: Ion. gladness of heart, rejoicing, Eup.161, Call.Fr.2 P., Plu.2.713d, Aret.SD1.5, Chor.in Rev.Phil.1.225: pl., Ph.2.548, Luc.Abd.5, D.C.47.1

θυμίασις.definition: fumigating, Dsc.1.98, Antyll. ap; passing off in fumes, Arist.Mete.387a30; Porph.Abst.2.5

θυμιατήριον.definition: vessel for fumigation, Aë.9.41; name of the constellation Ara, Eudox. ap.Hipparch.1.11.6, Ptol.Tetr.28, etc

θυμιατίζω.definition: = Gp.6.13.3:—Med., ib.6.12.1 good for burning as incense, Pl.Ti.61c

θυμιάω.definition: Ion.aor. Hippon.92, Hdt.6.97:—Med; smoke, fumigate, PMag.Par.1.2970:—Med., Hp.ll.cc.:—Pass., Arist.HA623b20

θυμίζω.definition: taste of thyme, Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.32:—Pass., to be embittered, Hsch

θυμοβόρος.definition: eating the heart, Il.19.58, al.; Alc.Supp.23.10; A.R.4.1666; cj. for in A.Ag.103

θυμοδακής.definition: biting the heart, Od.8.185; AP9.77 : in late Prose, Aret.CA1.1, cf. Jul.Or.2.96a

θυμοειδής.definition: high-spirited, Hp.Aër.12; opp; passionate, hot-tempered, opp. ib.375c

θυμοκατοχέω.definition: nurse anger, cj. for in Epicur.Sent.Vat.62

θυμοκάτοχος.definition: restraining anger: neut. as Subst., spell for this purpose, PMag.Lond.121.941, PMag. Osl.1.35. PMag.Par.1.467, 831; PMag.Leid.W.6.38

θυμολεοντοφθόρος.definition: bold enough to slay a lion, PMasp.2iii22

θυμολέων.definition: lion-hearted, of Achilles, Il.7.228, Hes.Th.1007; of Ulysses, Od.4.724; of Hercules, 11.267, cf. Ar.Ra.1041

θυμόμαντις.definition: prophesying from one's own soul, A.Pers.224 ; cf

θυμομαχέω.definition: to be angry, Plb.9.40.4; fight desperately, D.S.17.33; contend obstinately, D.H.5.11

θυμοξάλμη.definition: drink of thyme, vinegar, and brine, Dsc.5.16

θυμόσοφος.definition: wise from one's own soul, i.e. naturally clever, Id.Nu.877, Plu.Art.17; of animals, Arr.Ind.14.4, Ael.NA16.15; ib.3; Plu.2.970e

θυμοφθορέω.definition: to be tormented in soul, S.Tr.142

θυμοφθόρος.definition: destroying the soul, life-destroying; heart-breaking, Od.4.716; 10.363; Hes.Op.717; of persons, troublesome, annoying, Od.19.323; cf

θυμοφονέω.definition: to be in the death-agony, gloss on Hsch

θυμόω.definition: make angry, provoke, LXXHo.12.14: once in; Med. and Pass., 2sg. Ar.Ra.584: fut. A.Ag.1069, LXXJb.21.4, Phld.Ir.p.89W.: aor. E.Hel.1343 , more freq. Hdt.3.1, al.; part. E.Ph.461, Pl.Lg.931b: pf. inf. Hdt.3.52, A.Fr.478…

θυνέω.definition: = only impf., dart along, Hes.Sc.[210]; ib.156, cf. 257; ib.286, cf. eund.Cat.Oxy.1358Fr.2.20

θύννα.definition: female tunny, f.l. in Hippon.35.2: Antiph.129.4, Archestr.Fr.37.1

θυννάζω.definition: spear a tunny-fish, strike with a harpoon, metaph., Ar.V.1087

θυνναῖος.definition: = an offering of the first tunny-fish caught, Antig. Car. ap. Ath.7.297e

θύννειος.definition: of the tunny-fish, pickled; tunny-fishery, IG4.752.7

θυννίς.definition: young female tunny, prob. l. in Hippon.35.2, Epich.74, Cratin.161, Stratt.12, Archestr.Fr.37.1, Arist.HA543a9, al

θυννοθήρας.definition: tunny-fisher, title of Mime by Sophron, Ath.7.303c, 306d, Ael.NA15.6

θυννοκέφαλος.definition: with the head of a tunny-fish, Luc.VH1.35

θυννοσκοπεῖον.definition: look-out to watch for shoals of tunnies, Str.5.2.6

θύνω.definition: only pres. and impf., = rush, dart

θυοδόκος.definition: receiving incense, full thereof, of the Delphic temple, E.Ion511, 1549; Id.Andr.1157, cf. Hsch

θυοσκέω.definition: make burnt-offerings, Hsch.; prob. in A.Ag.87

θυοσκοπία.definition: = haruspicina, used as etym. of Lyd.Mag.Prooem

θυοσκόπος.definition: inspecting the entrails, Hsch., Phot., v.l. in E.Rh.68

θυόω.definition: fill with sweet smells: pf. part. Pass. fragrant oil, Il.14.172; CypriaFr.4, cj. in h.Ap.184; Call.Lav.Pall.63: aor. part. Hedyl. ap. Ath.11.486b.— Ep. word

θυράζω.definition: aor. inf. thrust out of doors, Hsch

θυραῖος.definition: absent, abroad, A.Ag.1608, Ch.115; to come from abroad, E.Ion702 ; in the public eye, opp. Id.Med.217

θυραυλέω.definition: live in the open air, camp out; wait at another's door, of visitors, POxy.471.72 ; freq. of lovers waiting on their mistresses, Plu.2.759b, Ph.1.306, etc.; Plot.6.5.10

θυραυλία.definition: living out of doors, camping out; waiting at the door, of lovers, in pl., Ph.1.155, Philostr.Ep.29: sg., Luc.Merc.Cond.10

θύραυλος.definition: living out of doors, of shepherds, Hsch

θυρεοειδής.definition: shield-shaped: the thyroid cartilage , Gal.2.839, UP7.11, al.; Str.17.2.2; prob. for in Hippiatr.40

θυρεοφορέω.definition: to be armed with the oblong shield, Plb.10.13.2

θυρεοφόρος.definition: armed with such a shield, LXX1 Ch.12.24, Plb.10.29.6, Ascl.Tact.1.3, Plu.Crass.25; cf

θυριδόω.definition: make a window, PTheb.Bank11.10 :—Pass., furnished with windows, BGU 1116.15

θυροκοπέω.definition: knock at the door, break it open, esp. as; metaph., knock as at a door, Plu.2.503a; Alciphr.3.70

θυροκοπία.definition: knocking at the door, Diph.128, Lib.Or.11.47

θυροκόπος.definition: knocking at the door, begging, A.Ag.1195

θυροποιός.definition: door-maker, Poll.7.111; nickname of the Comic poet Aristomenes, Hsch., Suid

θυρόω.definition: furnish with doors, IG12.24.7; ib.22.1046.16; . . Ar.Av.614 : metaph., X.Mem.1.4.6:—Pass., roofed and furnished with doors, Tab.Heracl.1.142, cf. IG 11.287 A172 , PAmh.2.51.14, 24 ; furnished with apertures, JHS41.195…

θυρσάζω.definition: bear or brandish the thyrsus, Lacon. part. gen. pl. fem. for Ar.Lys.1313

θυρσάριον.definition: Dim. of Plu.2.614a:—of vegetables, head, Orib.Fr.55

θυρσεχθής.definition: of Bacchus, prob. f.l. for with thyrsus-spear, Orph.H.45.5

θυρσοκόμος.definition: thyrsus-keeper, a play of Lysippus, Suid

θυρσόλογχος.definition: thyrsus-lance, Callix.2; as Adj., thyrsus-like arms, Str.1.2.8

θυρσομανής.definition: he who raves with the thyrsus, epith. of Bacchus, E.Ph.792 , Orph.H.50.8

θυρσοφορέω.definition: bear the thyrsus, D.S.4.3; assemble or lead companies with the thyrsus, E.Ba.557

θυρσοχαρής.definition: delighting in the thyrsus, Inscr.Magn.215a.23, AP3.1

θύρωμα.definition: doorway (including posts, sill; panel, tablet, Diotog. ap. Stob.4.1.96; Archyt. ap. eund.4.1.138

θυρών.definition: hall, antechamber, S.El.328, OT1242, Fr.649.23, IG11.158 A57 , Plu.Pyrrh.34, etc

θυσία.definition: Ion. prop. burnt-offering; mode of sacrifice, Hdt.4.60, cf. 2.39

θυσιάζω.definition: sacrifice, Strato Com.1.21; LXX2 Ch.7.5, 2 Es.6.3; dub. l. in Lys.6.4; OGI339.36 ; ib.199.36 ; D.S.4.3: abs., LXX1 Ch.21.28, al., IG3.74.16, etc.: title of mime by Herodas

θυσιαστήριον.definition: altar, ib.Ex.27.1, al., Ev.Matt.23.18, J.AJ8.4.1, Cod.Just.1.12.3.2

θυτήρ.definition: sacrificer, slayer, A.Ag.224,240 , S.Tr.613, al.: coupled with Call.Iamb.1.221

θυτήριον.definition: = as name of the constellation Ara, Arat.403, Q.S.4.554

θύτης.definition: sacrificer or diviner, SIG589.18 , D.S.17.17, Onos.10.25, Arr.Epict.1.17.18, IG14.617.6 , App.Hisp.85, Hdn.4.12.3: Thess. IG9.1234

θύω.definition: impf. Ep. Od.15.222, Ion; Act., offer by burning meat or drink to the gods , . . , Il.9.219, cf. Aristarch. ap. Sch.ad loc., Com.Adesp.7D. ; of a drink-offering, Od.14.446, cf. 15.260; so made an offering of cheese, 9…

θύωμα.definition: that which is burnt as incense: pl., spices, Heraclit.67, Semon.16, Hdt.2.40,86, Luc.Syr.D.20

θυωρίς.definition: a table for offerings, Poll.4.123; cf

θωάω.definition: penalize, fine, IG12.4.7,12:—Andania Michel995 D19:—Cret. GDI4977 :—Pass., , IG9.333.9

θωμίζω.definition: whip, scourge, Anacr.21.10, cf. EM459.54:—also, bind, Hsch., Suid

θωπεία.definition: flattery, E.Or.670, Jul.Or.3.102c, etc.: pl., Ar.Eq.890; Pl.Lg.906b; ib.633d

θώπευμα.definition: piece of flattery, Ar.V.563: in pl., endearments, E.Supp.1103; flatteries, Pl.R.590c, Plu.2.823c:—Dim. bits of flattery, Ar.Eq.788

θωπεύω.definition: flatter, wheedle, S.OC1003, 1336, E.Heracl.983, Ar.Ach.657, Eq.48; be it thine to flatter thus, S.El.397; Pl.Tht.173a; Aeschin.3.226; Phld.Rh.2.170S.; to be a time- server, Ps.-Phoc.93; serve others , PSI5.525.16 ; of…

θωρακεῖον.definition: = II, breastwork, parapet, or; gunwale of a trireme, IG22.1604.31

θωρακίζω.definition: prose form of arm with a; generally, cover with defensive armour, X.Cyr.6.1.29; . . Ephipp.14.10: metaph., of wild boars, to sheathe themselves in mud, preparatory to fighting, Arist.HA571b16; of the ichneumon, Str.17…

θωράκιον.definition: Dim. of Luc.Par.49; breastwork, parapet, Plb.8.4.4, D.S.17.44 , J.BJ5.7.4, Ph.2.324; shield for those who worked the battering-ram, Ath.Mech.18.11; or for those who attempted to burn the enemy's engines, D.S.14.51; Me…

θωρακίτης.definition: soldier with breast-armour only, Plb.10.29.6, al.:—fem. as Adj., cuirass-belt, prob. in PPetr.3p.12

θωρακοποιός.definition: maker of breastplates, X.Mem.3.10.9, IG22.1261.3, PTeb.278i8

θωρακοπώλης.definition: dealer in breastplates, Ar.Pax in Ind. personarum

θωρακοφόρος.definition: Ion. wearing a breastplate, cuirassier, Hdt.7.89,92, 8.113, X.Cyr.5.3.36, Jul.Or.2.63c; D.C.47.43

θωρήσσω.definition: fortify with drink, Hp.Epid.2.5.10; Nic.Al.32; Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.23; make drunk, intoxicate, Thgn.842:—Med. and Pass., get drunk, Id.470: abs., Id.413, Pi.Fr.72; Hp.Morb.4.56, cf. Duris27 J

θωΰσσω.definition: of a dog, bark, bay, Hom.Fr.25; of a gnat; c. acc. pers., call on, call, . . Id.OC1624: c. dat., shout to dogs, E.Hipp.219 , cf.Ba.871

θαρσούντως.definition: Att. Adv. from gen. pres. part. of boldly, X.Smp.2.11, Phld.Rh.1.325S., Jul.Or.2.83a; D.C.53.3

θατέρως.definition: Adv. in the other way, Simp.in Ph.210.10

Θείβαθεν.definition: Adv., Boeot.for from Thebes, Ar.Ach.862:— at Thebes, ib.868 codd

θειόθεν.definition: Adv., I.4) from the Emperor, Just.Nov.82.9

θεόθεν.definition: Adv. from the gods; by the will or favour of the gods, Pi.O.12.8, P.11.50, A.Th.324, Pers.101 , etc.; by the gods, S.Ant.584

θην.definition: enclit. Particle chiefly Ep. and Dor., rare in Trag., A.Pr.928:—in truth, I ween, freq. ironical, Il.13.620; 17.29, cf. 21.568; strengthd., in very truth, 11.365, 13.813; surely not, 2.276, Od.5.211; 3.352; Il.21.568:…

Θρᾳκιστί.definition: Adv. in Thracian fashion; in the Thracian dialect, Str.7.6.1, A.D.Adv.162.4

θύραζε.definition: Adv., for to the door, and so; generally, out, Il.5.694, Od.15.451, etc.; . . a way of getting out of the sea, 5.410; Il.16.408, cf. 21.237; 18.447; Ar.Ach.359; Id.Eq.365; Id.V.70; empty outside, Id.Fr.306; E.Fr.1063.…

θύραθεν.definition: Adv.from outside the door: and generally; outside the door, outside, E.Fr.1063.4; Arist.Resp.480a30, cf. PA642b1, foreigners, the enemy, A.Th.68, 193

θύραθι.definition: Adv. at the door, EM25.17:—Ep. outside, I was soon out , Od.14.352

θύρηφι.definition: Ep. dat. of used as Adv., outside, Od.9.238, Hp.Superf.2, etc.; opp. Od.22.220; or Hes.Op.365, Naumach. ap. Stob.4.23.7
